sentences.text:
2. Heard learned counsel for the parties.
3.

FIR in crime No. 147/2023 was registered by the Kirugavalu Police Station initially for offence punishable under Sections 498A and 504 read with Section 34 of IPC against petitioner and 3 others based on the first information dated 13.12.2023 received from Rudregowda - father of the deceased Madhushri.
During the course of investigation the petitioner was arrested on 13.12.2023 and remanded to judicial custody.
Investigation of the case is completed and charge sheet has been filed against NC: 2025:KHC:10391 4 persons.
Bail application filed by the petitioner before the trial Court in S.C. No. 39/2024 was rejected on 06.08.2024 and therefore, he is before this Court.

4. Learned counsel for petitioner submits that considering the allegations found in the first information it becomes doubtful that the daughters of the petitioner are the eye witnesses to the incident in question.
He submits that the elder daughter of the petitioner has not made any allegation against the petitioner in her statement recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C.
Petitioner has no criminal antecedent and he is in custody since 13.12.2023 and accordingly prays to allow the petition.

sentences.text: 5. Per contra learned HCGP has opposed the petition.
He submits that death had taken place in the house of the petitioner and his minor daughters are the eye witnesses to the incident in question.
There is strong material evidence against the petitioner.
Accordingly he prays to dismiss the petition.

6. A perusal of the material on record would go to show that the marriage of the petitioner with the deceased NC: 2025:KHC:10391 was solemnized in the year 2013 and they had 2 minor daughters who were aged about 9 years and 3 years respectively as on the date of the incident.

In the first information submitted by the father of the deceased he has alleged that his daughter was ill treated in her matrimonial house by accused Nos. 1 to 4 and they were demanding additional dowry from her and it is in this background they had conspired and committed her murder.
From the aforesaid it is apparent that only on suspicion accused Nos. 1 to 4 were arraigned as accused in the present case.
After investigation is completed charge sheet has been filed against all the accused named in the FIR.

The allegation in the charge sheet is that the petitioner was quarrelling with the deceased on petty issues and on 12.12.2023, at about 10.30 pm, after quarrelling with her, he had assaulted her with an iron rod on her head and had committed her murder.
C.W.3 and C.W.4 who are the minor daughters of the petitioner are the alleged eye witnesses to the incident.
C.W.3 is aged about 3 years and C.W.4 is aged about 9 years.

C.W.4 has NC: 2025:KHC:10391 not made any allegation against the petitioner in her statement recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C., about he assaulting the deceased on the date of incident with an iron rod.
The petitioner has no criminal antecedents and he is in custody since 12.12.2023.
The prosecution in all has cited 28 charge sheet witnesses and till date only 2 charge sheet witnesses have been examined.

Considering the nature of allegations found in the charge sheet against the petitioner and also the statement of C.W.4 who is the elder daughter of the petitioner, I am of the opinion that petitioner who is in custody has made out case for grant of regular bail.
7. The petition is allowed.
